limits: Synthetic execution does not establish task accuracy or universal speedups.

Each run requests an H100 and runs cases serially; Modal supplied an H200 for final-performance. Actual hardware is retained per report. CPU allocation is 4 and actual Torch thread counts are in each report. Modal CPU identity is only x86_64; no CPU model claim.
CPU and accelerator RNG streams differ. Matched-spike/weight numerical gates are separate from pipeline timing.
Cold epochs can reuse compiler caches and earlier numerical gates; raw validation/first-execution and cold timings are retained.
Source snapshots span Git heads and source revisions. Exact source hashes and settings are retained per report. Later recording/profile fixes have dedicated final runs.
Earlier profiler windows prepared one extra batch before stopping; use final_profile and recording_final for bounded-window counts.
Profiler copy tables describe exported events. Missing rows do not establish zero transfer; the final eager diagnostics observe both input payloads.
CUDA Graph timing starts from resident inputs and covers a fixed-shape compiled training step only; no public replay mode is enabled.
PyTorch 2.10.0 pinned-host allocator counters include negative freed counts and active bytes above owned bytes; raw values are retained but pinned-host peak values are unreliable.
CPU RSS is process-lifetime high water. Device allocator peaks include cold work; pinned-host peaks can include cached blocks retained from earlier cases.
All failures, rejected optional precision settings and superseded harness probes remain retained. No failed case contributes a throughput result.

Harness compares optimizer step on candidate device; cuda-949166eb27dc passed.
